bull.tldr: Modarabas showed unusually broad one-day participation: 16 of 19 members advanced and 9 remain above the 50-day average. FPJM led with a 68.76% 20-day gain, but the sector's -2.98% median 20-day return and thin fundamental coverage limit the recovery case.
bull.case: The strongest constructive evidence is breadth rather than valuation. Sixteen of 19 names advanced on the latest session and 9 of 19 sit above the 50-day average, indicating that the move was not confined to one ticker. FPJM is up 68.76% over 20 sessions, while PIM, SINDM and FTMM are also up 55.85%, 24.76% and 19.74%. The sector's median payout is only 33.33%, and FHAM combines a 4.55 P/E, 6.89% yield and +38.8% fair-value gap, providing one priced example of potential value support.

pillars.claim: Several members have positive medium-term momentum
pillars.evidence: FPJM +68.76%, PIM +55.85%, SINDM +24.76% and FTMM +19.74% over 20 sessions

pillars.claim: At least one priced name combines value and income support
pillars.evidence: FHAM P/E 4.55, fair_gap_pct +38.8%, yield 6.89% and payout 33.33%

bull.weakest_pillar: The momentum pillar is vulnerable because the sector median 20-day return is still -2.98%, FPJM is a single outlier, and most members have no valuation or income data.

bear.tldr: The one-day rebound does not repair the medium-term picture: Modarabas have a -2.98% median 20-day return, only 3 of 19 members carry valuation data, and just one member pays a recorded dividend. The best and worst 20-day returns span +68.76% to -30.94%.
bear.case: The sector's fundamental base is too thin for a high-confidence recovery call. Only 3 of 19 members have P/E or fair-value coverage; two of those three are overvalued, including WASL at a -91.1% fair-value gap and TRSM at -89.7%. Only one member is counted as a payer, so the 6.89% median yield is not a sector-wide income cushion. Price dispersion is severe: FPJM is up 68.76% over 20 days while FTSM is down 30.94%, and the sector median remains negative despite 16 advances in the latest session.

pillars.claim: Medium-term performance remains negative despite the rebound
pillars.evidence: returns.median_20d_pct = -2.98%; best FPJM +68.76% versus worst FTSM -30.94%

pillars.claim: Valuation coverage is sparse and mostly adverse
pillars.evidence: n_valued = 3 of 19; n_overvalued = 2 versus n_undervalued = 1; median_fair_gap_pct = -89.7%

pillars.claim: Income support is not broad enough to underwrite the sector
pillars.evidence: income.n_payers = 1 of 19; median yield 6.89% and median payout 33.33%

bear.attacks_bull: The bull's breadth argument is real but short-horizon: 16 advancing names coexist with a negative 20-day median, and the strongest named winners include thinly covered or low-liquidity members. FHAM's attractive figures cannot stand in for the other 18 members, while FPJM's +68.76% return is an outlier rather than sector-wide evidence.
bear.weakest_pillar: The valuation attack relies on only three priced names, so its negative conclusion cannot be generalized to the full 19-member sector without acknowledging the same coverage problem that weakens the bull case.

bull_rebuttal: The bear is right that coverage is the binding constraint and that the -2.98% median 20-day return has not been repaired. The remaining bull case is narrower: the 16-of-19 advancing count and 9-of-19 above-SMA50 count show that the latest move had breadth, while FHAM demonstrates that at least one priced member has both value and income support. That is evidence of a possible stabilization, not proof of a sector re-rating.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the 16-of-19 advancing session is followed by a positive median 20-day return and breadth above the current 9-of-19 above-SMA50 count.
Whether FPJM's +68.76% 20-day move holds while the sector median stops underperforming the KSE-100.
The scheduled WASL results on 2026-09-29 and FHAM results on 2026-10-28, including whether fresh filings expand reliable valuation and income coverage beyond 3 of 19 members.
dossier_gaps: Sixteen of 19 members have no P/E or fair-value coverage, so both valuation cases rest on a very small sample.
Only one of 19 members is counted as a dividend payer, limiting the usefulness of the sector income medians.
The dossier provides no sector-level liquidity aggregate, making it difficult to distinguish broad investable demand from thin-name price movement.
Macro drivers are empty and macro_joint_r2_pct is null, so the dossier does not quantify a global-factor explanation for the sector's returns.

house_view.tldr: Cautious, low conviction: Modarabas produced a broad +2.47% median one-day move with 16 of 19 advancing, but the median 20-day return remains -2.98%, valuation covers only 3 names, and income covers only one payer.
house_view.summary: The latest tape is constructive but not yet a repaired trend. Sixteen of 19 members advanced and 9 remain above their 50-day average, while FPJM, PIM, SINDM and FTMM posted strong 20-day gains. Against that, the sector median 20-day return is -2.98%, the return range is dominated by FPJM at +68.76% and FTSM at -30.94%, and only 3 members carry valuation data. Two of those three are marked overvalued, while only one member is counted as a payer. FHAM is a credible priced counterexample with P/E 4.55, +38.8% fair-value gap and 6.89% yield, but it cannot underwrite the rest of the roster. The desk therefore keeps a cautious, low-conviction view until the breadth improvement persists and the upcoming results add reliable coverage.
key_evidence: income.n_payers = 1 of 19; FHAM P/E 4.55, fair_gap_pct +38.8%, yield 6.89%, payout 33.33%
house_view.dissent: The strongest argument against caution is the breadth of the latest rebound. Sixteen of 19 members advanced and 9 of 19 sit above the 50-day average, which is materially stronger than a one-name move; the gains in FPJM, PIM, SINDM and FTMM indicate several independent pockets of demand. The negative median 20-day return may therefore be a lagging statistic after a sharp rotation rather than evidence that the rebound is failing. The bear's valuation case is also internally limited: 2 overvalued names out of 3 priced members cannot establish that the other 16 are expensive when they have no coverage, and FHAM is a concrete counterexample with low P/E, positive fair-value gap and a moderate payout. If the next dossier keeps breadth near or above 9 of 19, expands valuation coverage, and the sector median turns positive, the cautious stance would be too restrictive. That is why conviction remains low rather than high.

claims.text: Modarabas underperform the KSE-100 over the 30-day window from 2026-09-19 through 2026-10-19 unless the sector's breadth remains above 9 of 19 and its median 20-day return turns positive.
